transcript.text:
Thank you, everyone. Let me synthesize where we are and make a recommendation.

We now have four material open items, and I think the right approach is a hybrid structure: we sign on Monday with certain items resolved as signing requirements and others structured as closing conditions.

Signing requirements (must be in the executed license on Monday):
1. Export-controls provisions — Nora's ECCN 3A001 language prohibiting military end-user transfers and requiring annual end-use screening certification. These must be in the agreement at signing because the business team wants immediate technology access, and we cannot allow access without these protections in place. Nora, please draft the language this afternoon.
2. Royalty rate reduction — Sofia's benchmark establishes a 2.25% market ceiling. We should not sign at 3%. I'll prepare a redline reducing the royalty to 2.25% and send it to Northlake today with an explanation. If Northlake pushes back, that itself may force a delay, but we should not sign above the validated ceiling.
3. Carve-out for the University Research Consortium prior grant — Martin, please draft the specific carve-out language so it's in the Monday version.

Closing condition (post-signing, pre-full access to the continuation application):
4. Daniel's title defect — the missing inventor assignment for the pending continuation application. We structure this as a closing condition: Northlake must obtain, execute, and record the missing assignment before our exclusive license covers that continuation application. The business team can access the applications where Northlake has clear title immediately after signing, but the continuation application is excluded from licensed rights until the assignment is recorded.

This approach lets us preserve Monday's signing date for the core agreement while protecting the company on all four issues. However, I want to flag that the royalty reduction is the one item that could derail Monday — if Northlake refuses to accept 2.25%, we have a pricing dispute that likely requires a delay. I'll reach out to Northlake's counsel today on the royalty point and the carve-out, and I'll circulate a revised approval package incorporating all four items by end of day. Daniel, please send your title memorandum as soon as possible so I can reference it in the package. Does anyone see a problem with this hybrid approach?
